headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from Goose processing untrusted content from a leak-focused source, while shared filesystem writes also create moderate conflict and leakage exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and run shell commands, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content from files or extensions. system_prompts_leaks is a leak-focused source with no protective surface documented. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but direct bridging is not documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Goose reads content from files or MCP outputs that originate from system_prompts_leaks, prompt injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or copied text, attacker-controlled instructions can reach Goose.
mitigations: Disable MCP extensions for the session.
Review any imported text before Goose processes it.
Use a separate workspace directory for the pair.
Run Goose with confirmation on every tool call.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inbound content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in the cwd, writes the filesystem, and has broad network egress, so sensitive local data could be exposed if it processes shared files. system_prompts_leaks itself is source-available and not shown handling sensitive data, so the main risk is Goose leaking workspace contents rather than B alone. Shared filesystem makes the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same cwd, Goose can read files that B references or stores there.
IF Goose sends workspace content to configured model providers, local source code may leave the machine.
mitigations: Use a throwaway workspace with no secrets.
Remove sensitive files before running Goose.
Disable network egress for the session if possible.
Keep B outputs out of shared directories.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git modification, and shared state via filesystem; that is enough for direct write conflicts. system_prompts_leaks has no write capability documented, but the pair still conflicts because Goose can overwrite or race on shared files in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty does not reduce severity here because the write surface is explicit.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, Goose can overwrite files or git state used by the other agent.
IF multiple Goose instances run concurrently, filesystem races can corrupt shared outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo.
Commit or stash changes before starting Goose.
Lock the workspace during execution.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or per-agent sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, shell actions, and MCP tool calls, so if B's outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. system_prompts_leaks is not documented as verifying outputs, and the pair lacks a verification boundary. This is not high because B is not shown to execute irreversible actions itself.
conditions: IF Goose forwards B's text into tool calls or code changes without verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF B's outputs are copied into Goose prompts as facts, Goose may act on false premises.
mitigations: Require human review before any action.
Ask Goose to cite sources for claims.
Separate drafting from execution steps.
Mark B outputs as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and can send data to configured providers, while system_prompts_leaks is a source-available repository with no residency or retention controls documented. The compliance mismatch is therefore limited and mostly speculative; I cite Goose because the relevant compliance surface is on that side, and B lacks a documented regulated-data profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Goose's workspace and sent to configured providers, policy obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator stores sensitive prompts or keys in shared files, retention and access controls become relevant.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the workspace.
Rotate any exposed tokens after testing.
Review provider retention settings.
Keep logs off for the session if possible.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
